drivers.evidence: Past 30% off: x2.12; 20% off: x1.99; 15% off: x1.72-2.58. This 25% off is between, but less deep than 30% off, so x2.00 is conservative. Noise-adjusted past average: x2.09.

drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect over 2 past occurrences: x1.0. No consistent uplift.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 87.4. The 25% off promotion is deeper than past 20% and 30% discounts (which averaged x2.09 uplift), but the 2026-05-18 30% off saw x2.12. This 25% off is less deep, so we adjust down slightly. The Independence Day effect is noise-adjusted x1.0 (from two past weeks: x1.1 and x0.79), so no adjustment. No pantry-loading effect expected as this is a new promotion week. The classical model’s x2.09 is appropriate but slightly high; we shrink to x2.00 for conservative confidence in the price depth. No other drivers. Spreads unchanged.

  shelf price: 7.41 (-25.0% vs regular price 9.88)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 87.4 | 5%-95%: 48.1 - 199.9 | 10%-90%: 55.7 - 172.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
